chapter_name_en: Cosmogony, Geography, and Dimensions of the Creation
note: The Surya Siddhanta names seven patalas below the earth but gives them no names, and it has no table of seven upper lokas at all. The named patalas and lokas familiar from the Puranas are deliberately not included here.

inquiries.question: Of what measure is the earth, of what form, how supported, how divided?
How are there in the earth seven interterranean (patala) earths?
How does the sun cause the varying distinction of day and night?
Why are the day and night of the gods and of the demons opposed to one another?
Why does the day of the Fathers consist of a month, but that of mortals of sixty nadis?
Whence is it that the regents of the days, years, months and hours are not the same?
The orbits of the planets and stars — what are their heights, intervals, dimensions and order?
Why are the sun's rays hot in summer and not in winter, and how far do they penetrate?
How many modes of measuring time (mana) are there, and how are they employed?

creation_sequence.act: Having created the waters, deposited energy in them.
That energy became a golden egg, enveloped on all sides in darkness.
In it was manifested the everlasting one — the golden-wombed, called Aditya as the first existence, and the sun as generator.
Three quarters remaining immortal and secret, one quarter manifest, he produced Brahma, the principle of consciousness.
Bestowing the Vedas on Brahma, established him within the egg as grandfather of all worlds.
Wearing the form of consciousness, produced mind; from mind the moon, from the eyes the sun.
From mind the ether, and thence in succession wind, fire, waters and earth — the five elements, by the successive addition of one quality.
Agni and Soma — the sun and moon — then Mars and the rest, produced in succession from the elements.
Dividing himself twelve-fold, produced the signs; and twenty-seven-fold, the asterisms.
Wrought out the whole animate and inanimate creation, from the gods downward, from the upper, middle and lower currents.
Fashioned the distinctive character of each — of the planets, asterisms and stars, of the earth and the universe, of gods, demons, mortals and the Perfected.

patalas.description: Seven cavities within the earth-globe, the abodes of serpents (naga) and demons (asura), endowed with the savor of heavenly plants, delightful. The text neither names them nor gives their depths.

reference_places.name: Meru
reference_places.note: A mountain of gold passing through the middle of the earth-globe and protruding on either side; at its upper end are Indra, the gods and the Great Sages. Degrees of latitude at Meru are ninety.

reference_places.name: Vadavamukha
reference_places.note: The lower end of Meru, where the demons (asura) have their place, each the enemy of the other.

reference_places.name: Lanka
reference_places.note: The prime meridian of the treatise; 'at Lanka' is its ordinary phrase for a situation of no longitude or no latitude.

reference_places.name: Yamakoti
reference_places.note: A quadrant of the earth's circumference eastward, famed for walls and gateways of gold.

reference_places.name: Siddhapura
reference_places.note: The city of the Perfected (siddha), who dwell there free from trouble.

reference_places.name: Ujjayini
reference_places.note: Avanti, the modern Ujjain. Its situation is what actually fixes the prime meridian; the meridian is nevertheless named after Lanka.

regents.rule: Reckoning downward from Saturn, in the order of SS.12.31.
Counting downward from Saturn, the fourth successively is regent of the day.
Reckoning upward from the moon are found, in succession, the regents of the months.
The third, in like manner, is declared to be the regent of the year.
